origin.description: Nested bootstrap pivot for a correlation, and its tail probability.

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Observations with two columns. A data frame is used as an unnamed matrix.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Outer weight for each row. Rows are repeated round(n * w) times.

origin.details: Written for the double bootstrap in practical 5.5 of Davison and Hinkley (1997). The statistic is a weighted correlation and an influence variance. The outer weights select rows, the pivot is (correlation - t0) / sqrt(variance), and boot() with stype "w" draws the inner replicates. The second component is the proportion of inner pivots strictly below the outer pivot, divided by M + 1.
origin.value: A length-2 numeric vector: the outer pivot and the inner tail probability.
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
w <- rep(1/20, 20)
print(nested.corr(cd4, w, corr(cd4), 15))

translation.description: Nested bootstrap pivot for a correlation, and its tail probability.

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Two-column numeric array, one observation per row.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Outer weight for each row. Rows are repeated round(n * w) times, with ties rounded to even.

translation.details: The weighted correlation, the row repeats, and the pivot follow the source. The inner sample is drawn by boot.resample.boot with stype "w". Random draws use boot.rng, so set_seed matches set.seed. A non-finite inner pivot makes the probability NaN.
translation.value: A length-2 array: the outer pivot and the inner tail probability.
